problem.text: Given that the number we roll on a dice is even, what is the probability that our number is $2$.

steps.title: Where to start: the condition shrinks the outcomes
steps.body: The words "given that" tell you we already know something about the roll: it is even. So we only look at the outcomes where that is true and ignore the rest. This is called conditional probability.

your_turn.prompt: On a standard six-sided die, which outcomes are even?
your_turn.answer: $2$, $4$ and $6$: three outcomes, all equally likely.

steps.title: The formula
steps.body:
Let $A$ be "the roll is $2$" and $B$ be "the roll is even". The probability of $A$ given $B$ is
$$P(A \mid B) = \frac{P(A \text{ and } B)}{P(B)}$$
Careful: the answer is not $P(A) = \frac{1}{6}$, because that ignores what we were told.

your_turn.prompt: What is $P(B)$, the probability that a roll is even?
your_turn.answer: $\frac{3}{6} = \frac{1}{2}$, since $3$ of the $6$ faces are even.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: Rolling a $2$ already means the roll is even, so $P(A \text{ and } B) = P(A) = \frac{1}{6}$. Then $P(A \mid B) = \frac{1/6}{1/2} = \frac{1}{3}$. This matches the direct view: $2$ is one of the three equally likely even outcomes. The answer is **$\frac{1}{3}$**.
